title: Pack relevant imports into sutra_read symbol responses
description:
When sutra_read returns a symbol (function, method, etc.), include the file's import statements that are relevant to that symbol. Currently the agent has to separately read the file header or call sutra_deps to understand what a function depends on — this is a round-trip that's needed ~80% of the time.

Inspiration: archex's CodeChunk.imports_context field, which packs relevant imports alongside each code chunk.

sutra already parses imports at index time, so the data is available — this is about including it in the read response.

acceptance_criteria.text: sutra_read of a function includes relevant import statements in the response
Only imports referenced by the symbol body are included (not the entire file header)
imports field is included by default, suppressible via parameter
No meaningful latency regression on sutra_read

implementation_plan:
1. In the sutra_read handler, when returning a symbol, look up the file's parsed imports from the index.
2. Filter to imports that are referenced within the symbol's body (name matching against the import's imported identifiers).
3. Include an `imports` field in the response JSON — array of import statement strings, or a single string block.
4. Keep it opt-out (included by default) since it's typically small and almost always useful. Add `imports=false` param to suppress if needed.
execution_record: Implemented as planned. One discovery during testing: glob imports (`use super::*;`) from test modules were leaking into responses because they're unconditionally included. Fixed by scoping glob and Dart imports to only those preceding the symbol (positional filter). Derive-attribute types (e.g. `Deserialize`, `JsonSchema`) are not captured because sutra's tree-sitter parser records struct start_line at the `pub struct` line, not the `#[derive]` — this is a pre-existing parser limitation, not introduced here."
